subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style question on atomic structure, then mark my answer against the CCEA spec.
promptWeak: Explain atomic structure for GCSE CCEA Chemistry simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake.

questions.q: Which two subatomic particles are found in the nucleus of an atom?
questions.explain: The nucleus contains protons and neutrons. Electrons orbit the nucleus in shells.

questions.q: What is the relative charge on a proton?
questions.explain: A proton has a relative charge of +1. An electron is -1 and a neutron is 0 (neutral).

questions.q: Which particle has a relative mass so small it is treated as negligible?
questions.explain: The electron has a very small mass (about 1/1840 of a proton), treated as negligible. Protons and neutrons each have a relative mass of 1.

questions.q: What does the atomic number of an element tell you?
options: The number of protons plus neutrons
questions.explain: The atomic number equals the number of protons. In a neutral atom it also equals the number of electrons.

questions.q: The mass number of an atom is equal to the number of:
questions.explain: Mass number = number of protons + number of neutrons (the particles in the nucleus).

questions.q: An atom of sodium has atomic number 11 and mass number 23. How many neutrons does it have?
How many electrons are in a neutral atom of chlorine (atomic number 17)?
questions.explain: A neutral atom has equal protons and electrons, so 17 electrons.

questions.q: A magnesium ion Mg2+ has atomic number 12. How many electrons does it have?
questions.explain: Mg2+ has lost 2 electrons: 12 - 2 = 10 electrons. It still has 12 protons.

questions.q: A chloride ion Cl- has atomic number 17. How many electrons does it have?
Isotopes of an element are atoms with:
options: The same number of neutrons but different protons
Different numbers of protons and electrons
The same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons
The same mass number but different atomic number
questions.explain: Isotopes have the same atomic number (protons) but a different mass number, because they have different numbers of neutrons.

questions.q: Carbon-12 and carbon-14 both have 6 protons. How many neutrons does carbon-14 have?
questions.explain: Neutrons = 14 - 6 = 8. Carbon-12 has 6 neutrons; carbon-14 has 8.

questions.q: Why do isotopes of the same element have identical chemical properties?
options: They have the same number of neutrons
They have the same mass number
They have the same number of nucleons
They have the same electronic configuration
questions.explain: Chemical properties depend on the arrangement of electrons. Isotopes have the same number and arrangement of electrons, so they react the same way.

questions.q: Chlorine has two isotopes: 75% is chlorine-35 and 25% is chlorine-37. What is its relative atomic mass?
Relative atomic mass is a weighted average because:
options: Atoms are always the same mass
Elements exist as a mixture of isotopes in different abundances
Electrons contribute most of the mass
questions.explain: An element's atoms are a mixture of isotopes, so the Ar is the average mass weighted by the abundance of each isotope.

questions.q: What is the maximum number of electrons that can occupy the first electron shell?
questions.explain: The first shell holds a maximum of 2 electrons. The second and third shells each hold up to 8 (at GCSE).

questions.q: What is the electronic configuration of a sodium atom (atomic number 11)?
questions.explain: Sodium has 11 electrons filled as 2 in shell 1, 8 in shell 2, and 1 in shell 3: 2,8,1.

questions.q: An element has the electronic configuration 2,8,7. Which group of the periodic table is it in?
questions.explain: The number of electrons in the outer shell equals the group number. 7 outer electrons means Group 7.

questions.q: Rutherford's alpha-particle scattering experiment led to the conclusion that:
options: Most of the atom is empty space with a small dense positive nucleus
questions.explain: The scattering experiment showed most alpha particles passed through (empty space) while a few deflected sharply, showing a small dense positively charged nucleus.

questions.q: Where is almost all of the mass of an atom concentrated?
questions.explain: Nearly all mass is in the nucleus (protons and neutrons), because electrons have negligible mass.
